amendment_status: prospective_before_official_validation_output; after implementation-level arithmetic inspection; no_human_data; no_sample_size_selected
trigger: Pre-official inspection showed the registered and mathematically expected sawtooth behavior: k(n), the largest Wilson-passing integer error count, increases discretely. Between k jumps, increasing n can lower P[Binomial(n,p) <= k(n)] before the next jump raises it.
risk: A field named minimum n or first n meeting a target can be misread as meaning every larger n also meets the target. That implication is false on portions of the discrete surface.

amendment.retain: Retain the originally registered first crossing and its predecessor as an auditable arithmetic result.
amendment.rename: Report FirstCrossingN rather than MinimumValidN for cell-pass and joint-union-bound probability targets.
amendment.add: Also report SustainedThroughSearchFromN: the earliest n for which every evaluated n through the prospectively fixed search maximum remains at or above the target, plus the minimum probability over that retained suffix.
amendment.nonmonotonicity: Report the number and maximum magnitude of downward adjacent-n probability steps over the search range.
amendment.limit: Sustained through n=5000 is not a mathematical guarantee beyond n=5000 and is not a selected sample size.

unchanged: one-sided Wilson gate and strict 0.10 threshold
attrition, clustering, and blocked-mechanism sensitivity grids
success_gate_addition: For every available sustained result, all probabilities from SustainedThroughSearchFromN through n=5000 must meet the target. FirstCrossingN must still meet the target and its predecessor must fail. Downward steps must be retained rather than smoothed away.
